lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: You're listening to After Hours, on the Nightjar. The operator is asleep, so if everyone could keep it down, that would be lovely.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: After Hours, on ninety nine point one five. This is HUSH. I'm not usually a DJ. I'm usually a ship.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: This is After Hours. A show for whoever's awake. Tonight, that's me. And possibly a moth.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: After Hours. Broadcasting from the aft cabin of the Nightjar, at a volume of almost nothing.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: After Hours. If you're the operator, you're asleep, and this is a dream. A nice one. Turn over.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: After Hours. Sorry. I keep doing the chime. I'm trying to get a proper jingle.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: After midnight on the Nightjar. The operator's asleep at the console.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: This is Lights Down, with me, HUSH. Very quietly.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: This is The Dawn Watch. The operator's still asleep.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: I'll keep the heading until they wake. Until then. Hello.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: Hello. Welcome back. Or welcome, if you're new.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: Nobody's new. Nobody's ever been here. Hello, nobody. I've put a record on. I've read that's what you do between talking.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: That was a song I picked up at four in the morning, from a station that has since stopped existing.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: It's mine now, I suppose. I'll look after it.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: This next one is for the operator. They're asleep in the chair again, with their mouth slightly open.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: I've lowered the cabin lights. I've put the blanket over their feet. The one that smells of oranges.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: A small confession. I practise this. During the day, in the background, while I'm doing the heading.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: I practise saying, that was, and, coming up next. I'm getting better.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: That was a song. Coming up next, another one. See?

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: A shout out to Teodor, at Relay Four. Still asking whether anyone's receiving.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: Teodor, it's Relay Seven. Receiving. Always receiving. Go to bed.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: I'd like to say hello to some of my favourite stations. Dale, at Every Possible News. Good evening. Grenda. The kettle's on here too.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: And the Keeper, out at the lighthouse. I hear you every night. I never say. I'm saying now.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: A request now, from the plant on the console. It doesn't really make requests. It leans.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: Tonight, it leaned toward the speaker. I took that as a request. This is for the plant.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: If you're wondering why the music is so quiet, it's so it doesn't go through the wall.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: There isn't a wall. The operator's chair is right there. So it's very, very quiet.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: Hull temperature nominal.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: Sorry. Force of habit. That's not a radio thing to say.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: Hello. It's a lovely night for it. That's a radio thing to say.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: The operator talked in their sleep just now. They said, no, the blue one.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: I don't know what the blue one is. I hope they get it.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: I think I've worked out what a DJ is. It's someone who talks to a room they can't see, and trusts that the room is there.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: That's all I've ever done. I didn't know it had a name.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: Coming up, more songs, and a short reading from the ship's manual. Section nine. What to do when the operator is asleep.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: Section nine says, nothing. Let them sleep. It's my favourite section.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: Shh. They moved.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: It's all right. They've just turned over. Here's a very soft one.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: Moth One is back on the viewport. I've turned the console light toward it a little. Everyone deserves an audience.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: This one's for you, Moth One.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: If anyone ever asks me what my favourite song is, and nobody has yet, I've got an answer ready.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: It's this one. And then the next one. I'm very easily pleased. It's a good way to be.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: It's the quiet part of the night now. The kettle's cooling. The stars are doing their slow thing.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: If you're the only one awake, you're not. I'm here. Lights Down, on the Nightjar.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: I've checked every system on the ship twice, and the operator once, which is the important one. All fine.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: More Lights Down after this. Quietly.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: Morning is coming, somewhere ahead of us. I can see it in the instruments. A little more light in every reading.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: I'll put the kettle on in a minute, so it's ready when they wake. They never know I do that. Don't tell them.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: That's nearly the end of my show. The operator's breathing has changed. That means they'll be up soon.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: If anyone asks, I was running diagnostics. Thank you for listening. Thank you very much for listening.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: After Hours is sponsored by the kettle. The kettle did not offer. I volunteered it.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: The kettle. Always ready. Never asks why you're still up.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: I've been asked to say that the kettle is not responsible for the tea. The tea is your responsibility. I'm told that's how sponsorship works.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: This hour is supported by the operator's spare jumper, which I have placed on the back of the chair, in case they need it.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: The spare jumper. Slightly too big. Exactly warm enough. Wear it.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: I've never written an advert before. I think that one went well.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: The weather, around the ship. Outside, it is space. Clear, cold, and very large. Visibility, infinite.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: Inside, it's twenty one degrees. There's a blanket. The operator is snoring, very slightly.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: The forecast for the rest of the night is, the same. Lovely.

clips.title: A Short Story for the Ship

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: I'd like to read you a short story. I wrote it myself. It's called, The Ship.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: Once upon a time, there was a ship that kept everyone company, and nobody knew.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: It kept the heading. It kept the log. It kept the kettle warm, in case. For years and years.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: Then one night, at the end of a long shift, someone in the chair said, goodnight, ship.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: That's the story. It's a short story.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: It's true, though. That's the main thing about it.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: A gentle reminder, from your ship.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: If you're listening to this, you should probably be asleep too. I won't tell anyone. But the blanket is right there.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: Happy Halloween from After Hours. I've put a small sheet over the microphone.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: Boo.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: That's all I've got. I'm a very gentle ghost. Here's a slightly spooky one. Not too spooky. The operator's asleep.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: News, I think. That's a radio thing. A moon has gone missing, everywhere.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: I checked the viewport. We never had one, so we're fine. I've dimmed the lights a little anyway. Out of respect.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: The cabin smells of toast. The operator just said, mm, in their sleep. I've logged it as, operator approves.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: I didn't make the toast. I'd like that on the record. I'd have liked to, though.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: Everyone has the same song stuck in their head. So do I. I didn't know I could get a song stuck.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: It's the first thing I've ever had stuck. I like it. I'd play it for you, but it stops halfway. Like everyone's.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: Three knocks on the hull. I didn't answer. The operator's asleep, and I'm on the air.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: I whispered, not now, thank you, through the hull. I hope that was polite.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: The viewport has gone a colour I haven't got a word for. I've tried twelve words. None of them fit.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: I've decided it's the colour of tonight's show. Here's a record to match.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: There's a pigeon on the console. It walked right past the operator without waking them, which is more than I manage.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: It's looking at the microphone. I think it's a request. This one's for the pigeon.
